name: South Africa
dek: Cape Town International Airport, WMO 68816. Wet winters, dry summers.
paragraphs: The South African 1991–2020 submission has no Pretoria or Johannesburg file. The reference station is Cape Town International Airport, WMO 68816, height 42 m, so this is a Cape Town table with winter rain; the interior and the east coast are not this. January is midsummer.

The highest average high in the table is 27.3 °C, in February. The lowest average low is 7.4 °C, in July. The wettest month by the precipitation column is June, at 92.3 mm, and the driest is January, at 9.4 mm.

climate.caption: Reference station: Cape Town International Airport, WMO 68816. Not Johannesburg and not a national average.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3. The South African submission has no Pretoria or Johannesburg file.
climate.sourceTitle: WMO climate normals 1991-2020, Cape Town International Airport (68816)

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C, M and N, 230 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows South Africa at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: South African Tourism's page on getting around by car says South Africans drive on the left-hand side of the road, that seatbelts are compulsory, and that speed limits are in kilometres per hour.
driving.sourceTitle: SouthAfrica.net (South African Tourism), getting around by car

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: South African Tourism's know-before-you-go page for UK visitors says 10–15% is customary in restaurants and for tour guides. Its driving page adds that a small tip, around R5, is customary for a petrol attendant.
tipping.sourceTitle: SouthAfrica.net (South African Tourism), know before you go

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for South Africa, last reviewed August 25, 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Rand and the code ZAR for South Africa. It lists the same currency for Lesotho and Namibia alongside their own.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab gives South Africa one row, Africa/Johannesburg. zone1970.tab lists that zone on a row it shares with Lesotho and Eswatini; the zone name is the same in both files.
